title: Can the Railway hold back the final bill?

scenes.dialogue: Advocates, the Railway paid eighty five percent on account, against a contractor's test certificates. Can it still hold back the final payment?
scenes.shown: Advocates, the Railway paid 85% on account, against a contractor's test certificates. Can it still hold back the final payment?

scenes.dialogue: The work was done and certified complete. Yet the arbitrator rejected the claim, and the Commercial Court agreed. Can a Section Thirty Seven appeal change that?
scenes.shown: The work was done and certified complete. Yet the arbitrator rejected the claim, and the Commercial Court agreed. Can a Section 37 appeal change that?

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. A Chhattisgarh High Court bench of Honourable Justice Parth Prateem Sahu and Honourable Justice Sushma Sawant ruled.
In two thousand five, the Railway hired Teja Electricals to electrify a siding. Materials had to come from R D S O or CORE approved sources.
scenes.shown: In 2005, the Railway hired Teja Electricals to electrify a siding. Materials had to come from RDSO or CORE approved sources.

scenes.dialogue: The work was completed in May two thousand six. Eighty five percent was paid on account, and the final bill left a balance of over forty one lakh rupees.
scenes.shown: The work was completed in May 2006. 85% was paid on account, and the final bill left a balance of over ₹41 lakh.

scenes.dialogue: Then the Railway asked for the maker's test certificates for the steel masts. The reports came from a firm that had only galvanised them, so the bill was withheld.
The contractor said the sources were confirmed, and the on account payment proved compliance. The Railway said a Section Thirty Seven court cannot reweigh evidence.
scenes.shown: The contractor said the sources were confirmed, and the on-account payment proved compliance. The Railway said a Section 37 court cannot reweigh evidence.

scenes.dialogue: Before I tell you what the High Court decided, a quick request: follow LawWorld, and try India's all in one A I platform for advocates at lawworld dot A I.
scenes.shown: Before I tell you what the High Court decided, a quick request: follow LawWorld, and try India's all-in-one AI platform for advocates at lawworld.ai.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? An approved source was an essential term, not a formality, and the arbitrator's reading was a plausible view.
An on account payment is no acknowledgment of full compliance, nor an automatic waiver. The award was not perverse, and the contractor's appeal was dismissed.
